author: British Museum
title: British Museum collection record for Oc.2599

notes.text:
The collection already has the nonspecific handle `rapa-britanico` (“Rapa — Londres”), but its source gives no accession or distinguishing description. This catalogue entry cannot be matched to that handle, and several selected BM dance-paddles could fit it. The catalogue labels this combined field “Found/Acquired”; it is retained as source wording and is not treated as an independently established findspot. A separate “Production place” field is represented as made_at when present.

30 September 2026 identity review: ambiguous crosswalk to `rapa-britanico`; keep this catalogue source unlinked. The British Museum identifies Museum number Oc,+.2599 (https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/E_Oc-2599), a carved dance-paddle (rapa), 88 × 18 × 2.20 cm. Its accession history says A W Franks presented it on 18 September 1885; it was brought from Easter Island by a sailor, as part of the Oc,+.2595–2601 group. The description records a point at one end and a blade with raised curved lines ending in knobs. Oc,+.2598 shares that point-and-blade form and group history; Oc,+.2600 is a separately catalogued anthropomorphic paddle in the same group. The generic Arte row says only Rapa and Museo Britanico/Londres, with no accession or diagnostic detail. Resolution needs a primary description or image tied to that row, or a historical accession crosswalk.
